episodes.185606: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and early evening hours of the 4th, with two primary focusing boundaries to support the development across the area. An outflow boundary from earlier thunderstorm activity stretched across east-central Oklahoma, while a cold front moved into the area from the northwest. The air mass became moderately unstable, and the deep-layer wind shear was strong across the region, supporting the development of organized and persistent, intense thunderstorms. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to ping pong ball size, and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185726: Forcing and instability ahead of a low pressure system moving across the region spawned strong to severe thunderstorms and isolated waterspouts over portions of Lake Superior during the afternoon of the 5th.
episodes.185783: A lingering upper-level low enhanced convection over the adjacent coastal waters.
episodes.185843: Outer bands from Tropical Storm Philippe, which passed northeast of the islands resulted in heavy rain, river rises, lightning strikes and flooding across various sectors of the islands. Around up to 5 to 10 inches of rain fell over mainly eastern Puerto Rico from Oct 1st through October 5th.
episodes.186261: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the late morning and early afternoon hours of the 5th across northeastern Minnesota. While the storms were rather benign over land with reports of pea-sized hail, stronger wind gusts were reported over the waters of western Lake Superior. Gusts closer to shore were in the 40 to 55 mph range with gusts to 66 mph reported by two Great Lakes bulk carriers over the open waters of western Lake Superior.
episodes.186385: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front as it moved southward through South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.186458: A prolonged period of very heavy rainfall along with severe thunderstorms occurred on October 4th-5th across parts of Northeast Texas. Showers and thunderstorms with 1-3 inch per hour rainfall rates trained in the vicinity of a warm front, which was oriented across the Ark-La-Tex and in adjacent portions of Southeast Oklahoma and Northeast Louisiana. Deep convergence of moisture along the boundary resulted as the core of the low-level jet and associated moisture transport was directed due north from the Upper Texas coast. Other factors contributing to the heavy rainfall and severe storms included a sharp instability gradient with mean-layer CAPE values from 500-1500 J/kg, maximized precipitable water values from 2.0-2.2 inches and effective bulk shear of 25-30 knots. As a result, this area of Northeast Texas quickly became more favorable for increasing convective organization as multi-cell thunderstorms continued to train over the same areas from late morning throughout much of the afternoon and evening. Over time, flash flooding developed in areas impacted by 4-8 inch rainfall totals, most notably in and around the Texarkana metro area. Severe impacts from damaging wind gusts occurred farther south closer to the Interstate 20 corridor.
episodes.186588: The last day of an anomalous stretch of late-season severe weather across portions of the southwestern Great Plains. As a large tough continued to approach the region, strong shear, and rich low-level moisture aided in the development of numerous supercells across portions of the Permian Basin and Trans Pecos. Of note are supercells that impacted the Odessa and Fort Stockton areas with large hail.
episodes.186601: Thunderstorms formed over the Texas coastal plains ahead of a cold front during the morning hours of the 5th. Thunderstorms produced severe wind gust in the Victoria area.
episodes.186602: Thunderstorms formed along a cold front over south Texas on the 5th. Thunderstorms with locally heavy rainfall produced flooding in Laredo during the afternoon.
episodes.186603: A line of thunderstorms formed along a cold front during the morning hours of the 5th. The storms moved through the coastal waters of the Middle Texas coast during the late morning hours producing wind gusts from 35 to 40 knots.
episodes.186625: The young autumn's first cooling front arrived late on October 5th. Preceding the front, a rapidly developing cluster of strong thunderstorms formed in Willacy and Cameron County, aided by interaction with the sea breeze.  Torrential rains of nearly 4 inches in an hour in Brownsville just west of downtown created localized flash flooding, with more nuisance urban flooding in other parts of the city.
episodes.186627: A line/cluster of strong thunderstorms developed along the Coastal Bend and surged southward along the Lower Texas coast, producing gale-force wind gusts along Laguna Madre and the Lower Texas Gulf waters in spots out toward 60 nautical miles during the afternoon of October 5th.  Brief torrential rainfall and frequent lightning accompanied the storms, but there were no known damage reports.
episodes.186715: An isolated waterspout was observed near Duck Key as a convective cloud line developed near the middle Florida Keys.
episodes.189410: A cold front swept eastward from western Lower MI, northwestern IN, and vicinity to central Lake Erie and eastern OH during the early afternoon through early evening of the 5th. Clusters of multicell showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of the front moved north-northeastward over northeast OH and central and eastern Lake Erie, amidst weak MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear, during the late afternoon and early evening. One of the cells generated a gale-force peak convective wind gust at Fairport Harbor.
